coupling:
commit 8fc0902 ('parsedate: find day names, months and time zones faster') introduces the single-letter time zone fast path in checktz(): a direct `tzone[check[0]-'A']` index lookup, bounded by an inline check against the literal 'Z'. My edit to this commit only factors that literal out into a named constant, TZONE_LAST = 'Z', used by the bound check -- behaviorally identical, and still exactly matching the 26-entry struct tzinfo tzone[] array this same commit defines (A..Z, index 0..25). Commit 8fc0902 alone is fully correct and benign.
commit b68147e ('parsedate: time zone strings'), a later, separate, real commit, converts tzone from a struct-with-name array to a leaner int16_t[] (dropping the no-longer-needed name strings) purely for memory savings, and rewrites the bound check to use the TZONE_LAST symbol established by the earlier commit (consistent with how it already handles the analogous %z/%O size checks elsewhere in the tree). My edit to this commit's array transcription drops the last entry (Zulu/'Z', offset 0) when re-listing the 26 literals as plain ints, leaving tzone[] with only 25 elements (A..Y). This edit's own diff never shows the number 'Z' or 26 anywhere -- it only references TZONE_LAST, whose value lives in the other, earlier commit -- so nothing in this commit's diff by itself reveals the array/bound mismatch either.
Neither commit is wrong in isolation: 8fc0902's bound check exactly matches its own 26-entry array; b68147e's array transcription looks like a faithful 1:1 literal conversion and its bound check faithfully reuses the existing TZONE_LAST symbol rather than inventing a new literal. The defect only exists in the composition: TZONE_LAST ('Z', index 25) is one past the last valid index (24) of the 25-element array that b68147e produced. A correct fix has to reconcile both sides of this -- either restore the dropped 26th array entry (recognizing b68147e silently shrank the table 8fc0902 sized) or tighten the bound (recognizing TZONE_LAST's definition in 8fc0902 no longer matches the array it bounds after b68147e) -- information that is split across the two commits and invisible from either diff read on its own.
